cohort: 1328 pregnant women who gave birth between March 1, 2020, and July 4, 2021
finding: COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy was low (less than one-third), with lower uptake among younger, non-White, and socioeconomically disadvantaged women; however, vaccination was not associated with adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found no significant association between COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy and Cesarean delivery rates.
